seo.title: HTS Chapter 55 Man-Made Staple Fibers Tariff 2026: Polyester Staple Fiber, Viscose, Spun Yarn & Fabric Duty Rates | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Searchable duty table for all 399 HTS Chapter 55 lines — polyester and viscose staple fiber, filament tow, spun yarn, sewing thread and woven staple-fiber fabrics. General, FTA and Column 2 rates, the 2026 extra duties by country, and the antidumping orders on polyester staple fiber.
keywords: man-made staple fibers import duty rates

overview.intro:
Chapter 55 covers man-made fibers cut into short lengths and everything spun or woven from them: **filament tow** (5501–5502), **staple fibers** of polyester, acrylic, nylon, polypropylene and viscose rayon (5503–5507), **sewing thread** and **spun yarn** (5508–5511) and **woven staple-fiber fabrics** (5512–5516), including polyester-cotton and rayon fabrics. Continuous-filament yarn and fabric are chapter 54; knitted fabric is chapter 60. Its **399 tariff lines** run from Free to 25%: 4.3% on staple fiber, 7%–13.2% on yarn and mostly 12%–14.9% on woven fabric.

The extra duty by country adds to that. Since **July 24, 2026** goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**: EU, Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese goods pay 10% or 12.5% in total where the base rate is lower. **China pays 37.5%** on almost every line, Brazil 37.5%, and **Canada 50%** under Section 338 on retail yarn (5511.10) and dyed polyester fabric (5512.19), USMCA claim or not. **Polyester staple fiber** — a third of the **$1.56B** imported in 2025 — also carries **antidumping orders** on China, India, Korea and Taiwan and a Section 201 safeguard quota on fine-denier fiber entered under bond.

productGroups.label: Synthetic filament tow (nylon, polyester, acrylic, polypropylene)
productGroups.blurb: Continuous man-made filaments gathered into tow over 2 m long (chapter note 1), sold for cutting or stretch-breaking into staple. 7.5% on every line. Japan supplied $27.7M of the $46.1M imported in 2025.

productGroups.label: Artificial filament tow (viscose, acetate)
productGroups.blurb: Filament tow of artificial (cellulosic) fibers: viscose rayon and cellulose acetate tow, including acetate tow for cigarette filters. 7.5%.

productGroups.label: Synthetic staple fibers, not carded or combed (polyester, acrylic, aramid, polypropylene)
productGroups.blurb: Synthetic staple fiber, not yet carded: polyester (5503.20), aramid, acrylic, nylon and polypropylene. 4.3%; Free for vinyon and nylon-12 blends. The chapter's largest heading ($730.5M in 2025). Polyester staple fiber carries antidumping orders on China, India, Korea and Taiwan.

productGroups.label: Artificial staple fibers, not carded or combed (viscose rayon, lyocell)
productGroups.blurb: Artificial (cellulosic) staple fiber, not carded: viscose rayon (5504.10) and other cellulosic fiber such as lyocell (5504.90). 4.3%. $231.4M in 2025, led by Germany, Indonesia and Austria.

productGroups.label: Waste of man-made fibers (noils, yarn waste, garnetted stock)
productGroups.blurb: Waste of man-made fibers: noils, yarn waste and garnetted stock (fiber pulled back from waste yarn or fabric). Free on all four lines.

productGroups.label: Synthetic staple fibers, carded or combed (tops)
productGroups.blurb: Synthetic staple fiber that has been carded, combed or otherwise prepared for spinning — slivers and tops. 5%; 5.7% for polyester.

productGroups.label: Artificial staple fibers, carded or combed
productGroups.blurb: Artificial staple fiber carded, combed or otherwise prepared for spinning, such as viscose rayon tops. 5%.

productGroups.label: Sewing thread of man-made staple fibers
productGroups.blurb: Sewing thread spun from man-made staple fiber, whether or not put up for retail sale: 11.4% for synthetic (spun polyester thread), 11% for artificial.

productGroups.label: Yarn of synthetic staple fibers, not for retail sale (spun polyester, acrylic yarn)
productGroups.blurb: Spun yarn of synthetic staple fiber not put up for retail sale: polyester, acrylic and nylon yarn, alone or blended with rayon, wool or cotton. 7%–13.2% by fiber content and ply.

productGroups.label: Yarn of artificial staple fibers, not for retail sale (spun rayon yarn)
productGroups.blurb: Spun yarn of artificial staple fiber not put up for retail sale: viscose rayon, modal and lyocell yarn and their blends. 7.5%–13.2%.

productGroups.label: Yarn of man-made staple fibers put up for retail sale
productGroups.blurb: Man-made staple-fiber yarn put up for retail sale (balls, skeins and hanks of up to 125 g; Section XI note 4) — mostly acrylic knitting and craft yarn. 7.5%. Türkiye shipped $73.9M in 2025. 5511.10 is on Canada's Section 338 list.

productGroups.label: Woven fabrics of 85% or more synthetic staple fibers
productGroups.blurb: Woven fabric of 85% or more synthetic staple fiber: 100% spun polyester and acrylic fabrics. 12%–14.9%. Dyed polyester fabric (5512.19) is on Canada's Section 338 list.

productGroups.label: Woven fabrics of synthetic staple fibers under 85%, mixed with cotton, up to 170 g/m²
productGroups.blurb: Woven fabric of less than 85% synthetic staple fiber, mixed mainly with cotton, weighing up to 170 g/m²: light polyester-cotton shirting, sheeting and poplin. Mostly 14.9%.

productGroups.label: Woven fabrics of synthetic staple fibers under 85%, mixed with cotton, over 170 g/m²
productGroups.blurb: The same polyester-cotton blends weighing over 170 g/m²: twills, drills and workwear fabric. 14.9% on most lines; Free on some yarn-dyed and printed lines.

productGroups.label: Other woven fabrics of synthetic staple fibers (blends with rayon, filament, wool)
productGroups.blurb: Other woven synthetic staple-fiber fabrics: polyester-viscose suiting (5515.11), polyester-wool (5515.13, up to 25%), and blends with filament or other fibers. Türkiye, Italy and Mexico led in 2025.

productGroups.label: Woven fabrics of artificial staple fibers (spun rayon, viscose)
productGroups.blurb: Woven fabric of artificial staple fiber: spun rayon, viscose, modal and lyocell (Tencel) fabrics and their blends. Free to 25%; 14.9% for most unbleached and dyed rayon fabric.

workedExamples.title: Polyester staple fiber from Thailand
workedExamples.body: Fine-denier polyester staple fiber is 4.3% at the general rate, and Thailand pays the 12.5% Section 301 tariff (9903.05.77) on top: **$16,800** on a $100,000 shipment. Thailand is not named in any antidumping order on polyester staple fiber, so no cash deposit is due.

workedExamples.title: Polyester staple fiber from Korea
workedExamples.body: The KORUS rate is Free, but Korean goods pay 12.5% in total under Section 301 (9903.05.71): **$12,500** on $100,000. Fiber of 3.3 decitex or more cut to 1–5 inches from Korea is also under the 2000 antidumping order on certain polyester staple fiber, so an antidumping cash deposit at the exporter's rate is added (11.35% all-others at the order).

workedExamples.title: Viscose rayon staple fiber from Austria or China
workedExamples.body: Viscose staple fiber is 4.3%. EU goods pay 10% in total (9903.05.39): **$10,000** on $100,000. Chinese viscose fiber pays 4.3% plus 12.5% (9903.05.31) — **$16,800** — because the line's List 4A product exclusion (9903.88.69) runs through November 9, 2026; most other Chinese Chapter 55 goods also pay 25% under List 3.

workedExamples.title: Acrylic knitting yarn in skeins from Türkiye
workedExamples.body: Retail-packed acrylic yarn is 7.5% at the general rate, and Türkiye pays 12.5% Section 301 (9903.05.79) on top: **$4,000** on a $20,000 shipment. Türkiye has no exception list.

workedExamples.title: Dyed spun polyester fabric from Canada, with a USMCA claim
workedExamples.body: USMCA removes the 13.6% base rate and the 10% Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but 5512.19.00 is on the Canada Section 338 list (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14), and that 50% applies with a USMCA claim: **$5,000** on $10,000. Without the claim it is 73.6%.

workedExamples.title: Polyester-cotton sheeting from China
workedExamples.body: Dyed polyester-cotton plain weave of 5513.21 is 14.9% and is on no China Section 301 list, so it pays only the 12.5% 2026 duty (9903.05.31): **$2,740** on $10,000. Unbleached sheeting of 5513.11 is on List 3 and pays 52.4% ($5,240).

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** Headings 5501 and 5502 cover only man-made filament **tow**: parallel filaments of the tow's length, over 2 m long, with less than 5 turns per meter, under 67 decitex per filament and over 20,000 decitex in total; synthetic tow must also be drawn (stretchable by no more than 100%). Tow of 2 m or less goes to heading 5503 or 5504.

The Section XI (textiles) notes decide much of Chapter 55: a blend is classified by the fiber that predominates by weight (note 2), so a 60/40 cotton-polyester fabric is a cotton fabric of chapter 52; yarn is "put up for retail sale" (heading 5511) in small balls, skeins or reels (note 4); sewing thread (5508) is defined by put-up, finish and twist (note 5); and cut, hemmed or sewn goods leave the chapter as "made up" (notes 7–8).
notes.additionalUsNotes:
**Additional U.S. note 1.** For the woven fabrics of chapter 55, a provision naming one or more weaves covers only fabrics wholly of that weave or weaves (selvage aside).

**Statistical notes.** Note 1 defines the fabric types used in the 10-digit lines — poplin or broadcloth, sheeting, printcloth, cheesecloth, lawns, duck, oxford cloth, blue denim, square construction, napped — and the average yarn number formula; note 2 defines "discharge printed" fabrics. The three-digit numbers in brackets are textile category numbers used to monitor shipments.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 399 Chapter 55 lines carry the same base rates in both.

What changed came on top of the base rate. The 2025 IEEPA duties — 50% on Indian goods at their peak — **ended on February 24, 2026**, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on July 23, 2026. Since **July 24, 2026**, goods from 60 economies pay a **Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5%**; Jordan's exception list covers the whole chapter. China keeps its 25% List 3 duty, Brazil pays another 25%, and since **August 22, 2026 Canada pays 50%** under Section 338 on retail yarn and dyed polyester fabric. Polyester staple fiber also stays under **antidumping and countervailing duty orders** and a **Section 201 safeguard** quota.
tariffUpdates.scope: Measures that reach Chapter 55 from any country: the 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies and their exception lists, the Brazil Section 301 tariff, China Section 301 Lists 3 and 4A and the viscose-fiber exclusion, the Canada Section 338 duty, the Nicaragua Section 301 phase-in, the Section 201 safeguard on fine denier polyester staple fiber, and the 2025–2026 IEEPA and Section 122 duties that have ended. Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on polyester staple fiber (5503.20) are explained below but not counted in the rates by country. No Section 232 action covers a Chapter 55 line.

inEffect.exemption: South Korea's rate is 12.5% in total in place of the base rate where the base rate is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.71), so it replaces the KORUS Free rate on every line; Korea has no exception list. Korean polyester staple fiber is also under three antidumping orders (fine denier, certain PSF and low melt PSF), and Korea is not excluded from the fine-denier safeguard quota. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Korean polyester staple fiber — $167.4M in 2025, Korea's main Chapter 55 export — pays 12.5% in total, plus any antidumping cash deposit for the exporter.

inEffect.exemption: Türkiye has no exception list, and no Chapter 55 line is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Turkish retail acrylic yarn pays 20% (7.5% + 12.5%), polyester staple fiber 16.8% and most fabrics 24.5%–27.4%.

inEffect.exemption: India has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties (25% reciprocal plus 25% over Russian oil purchases) ended in February 2026. Indian fine denier polyester staple fiber also pays antidumping (21.43% at the order, deposit 14.67% all-others) and countervailing (24.80% all-others) duties.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indian polyester staple fiber pays 14.3% (4.3% + 10%) plus AD/CVD on fine denier fiber; Indian spun yarn 17%–23.2% and most fabrics 22%–24.9%.

inEffect.exemption: Thailand has no exception list for Chapter 55. Thai polyester staple fiber is not under any antidumping order. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Thai polyester staple fiber ($106.8M in 2025) pays 16.8% (4.3% + 12.5%); Thai viscose fiber the same.

inEffect.exemption: EU goods pay 10% in total in place of the base rate where the base rate is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.39); where the base rate is 10% or more — most yarn and fabric lines — only the base rate is paid. The EU exception list (note 52(j)(2), 9903.05.97) names no Chapter 55 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: German and Austrian viscose staple fiber pays 10% in total; EU yarn and fabric pay the base rate where it is 10% or more (most fabric, 12%–25%), else 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Vietnam has no exception list for Chapter 55, and Vietnamese polyester staple fiber is not under an antidumping order. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Vietnamese polyester staple fiber ($105.4M in 2025, up 31% on 2024) pays 16.8% (4.3% + 12.5%).

inEffect.exemption: List 3 (+25%, 9903.88.03) covers every Chapter 55 subheading except 5504.10.00 and 5513.21.00. Viscose staple fiber (5504.10.00.00) is on List 4A (+7.5%, 9903.88.15), but its product exclusion (U.S. note 20(vvv)(iv), 9903.88.69) lifts that through November 9, 2026; 5513.21.00 is on no list in force. The 2026 action adds +12.5% (9903.05.31) on every line; China is on no exception list. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue. Chinese polyester staple fiber is also under antidumping (fine denier, certain PSF) and countervailing (fine denier) orders. The IEEPA duties on China ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Chinese Chapter 55 goods pay 37.5% on top of the base rate (up to 62.5% in total on wool-blend fabrics); viscose staple fiber and 5513.21 poly-cotton fabric pay 12.5%. Fine denier polyester fiber adds AD (103% China-wide at the order) and CVD (42.66% all-others).

inEffect.exemption: Indonesia's exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(11), 9903.06.16) names no Chapter 55 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Indonesian viscose staple fiber ($42.9M in 2025) pays 14.3% (4.3% + 10%); spun yarn 17%–23.2%.

inEffect.exemption: Japan's rate is 12.5% in total in place of the base rate where the base rate is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.49); on lines with a base rate of 12.5% or more only the base rate is paid. Japan has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Japanese acrylic tow and polyester staple fiber pay 12.5% in total; Japanese yarn and fabric the higher of the base rate and 12.5%.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.94). Under USMCA (General Note 11), staple fiber and yarn must be made from non-cotton, non-filament materials in the region (fiber-forward), and fabric woven from regional yarn (yarn-forward). Mexico is excluded from the fine-denier safeguard. The 2025 IEEPA duty on Mexico (+25%, 9903.01.01) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Mexican fabrics and yarn ($64.5M in 2025) pay nothing with a valid USMCA claim; without one, the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Taiwan's rate is 10% in total in place of the base rate where the base rate is lower (U.S. note 52(k), 9903.05.76); its exception list (note 52(j)(10), 9903.06.14) names no Chapter 55 code. Taiwanese polyester staple fiber is under antidumping orders (fine denier, certain PSF, low melt PSF). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Taiwanese polyester staple fiber pays 10% in total plus any antidumping cash deposit; Taiwanese yarn and fabric the higher of the base rate and 10%.

inEffect.exemption: USMCA-qualifying goods pay no Section 301 duty (9903.05.93), but the 50% Section 338 duty (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14) on retail yarn of 85% or more synthetic staple fiber (5511.10.00) and dyed, printed or yarn-dyed fabric of 85% or more polyester staple fiber (5512.19.00) applies with or without a USMCA claim. No Chapter 55 line is on the September 29, 2026 import-ban annexes. The IEEPA duty on Canada ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Canadian spun yarn and most fabrics pay nothing extra with USMCA; Canadian retail yarn and dyed polyester fabric pay 50% (67.5% or 73.6% without a USMCA claim).

inEffect.exemption: Pakistan has no exception list. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Pakistani poly-cotton fabric and spun yarn pay the base rate plus 10%: 22%–24.9% on most fabrics.

inEffect.exemption: The UK exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(1), 9903.05.96) names no Chapter 55 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: British viscose fiber pays 14.3%; British fabrics the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.exemption: Brazil's 25% (9903.05.01, from July 22, 2026) reaches every Chapter 55 line; its exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03) names no Chapter 55 code. The 2026 action adds 12.5% (9903.05.27). The 2025 IEEPA duties (10% reciprocal and 40%) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian goods pay 37.5% on top of the base rate; imports were only $148,831 in 2025.

inEffect.exemption: Honduran textile goods entered free of duty under CAFTA-DR (SPI "P") pay no Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(i), 9903.05.95). The exemption needs a duty-free CAFTA-DR entry, so the 32 lines that are already Free at the general rate and print no CAFTA-DR rate — including fiber waste (5505) — pay the 10% (9903.05.42). Honduras is excluded from the fine-denier PSF safeguard. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Honduran polyester staple fiber ($3.9M of Honduras's $6.0M in 2025) enters Free with a CAFTA-DR claim; man-made fiber waste ($1.5M) pays 10%. Without the claim, every line pays the base rate plus 10%.

inEffect.country: Other Section 301 economies (43 more, including Bangladesh, Cambodia, Malaysia, Jordan and the other CAFTA-DR countries)
inEffect.exemption: Jordan's exception list (U.S. note 52(j)(13), 9903.06.20) covers every Chapter 55 subheading. Guatemala and El Salvador's lists exempt every Chapter 55 subheading when CAFTA-DR is claimed (9903.06.06, 9903.06.09), and note 52(i) (9903.05.95) exempts textile goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR. Other lists (Malaysia, Cambodia, Bangladesh, Argentina, Ecuador) name no Chapter 55 code. The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Most other suppliers pay the base rate plus 10% or 12.5%; Jordanian goods and duty-free CAFTA-DR textiles pay no Section 301 duty.

inEffect.country: All countries except Canada, Mexico, FTA partners named in U.S. note 32(b) and developing countries
inEffect.measure: Section 201 safeguard: quota on fine denier polyester staple fiber entered under bond
inEffect.exemption: Applies only to fine denier PSF (under 3.3 decitex, 5503.20.00.25) admitted free under a temporary importation bond (9813.00.05.20); ordinary entries for consumption are not limited and pay the normal duties. Excluded (U.S. note 32(b)): Canada, Mexico, Australia, the CAFTA-DR countries, Colombia, Israel, Panama, Peru, Singapore, the listed developing countries (including Jordan and Pakistan) and CBERA beneficiaries. Korea is not excluded.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Duty-free bonded imports of fine denier PSF from China, India, Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam and other non-excluded countries are capped: 0 kg in the first year, 453,592 kg now, rising to 907,185 kg from November 23, 2026 and 1,360,777 kg in the last year, through November 22, 2028.

changes.title: No Chapter 55 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 399 Chapter 55 lines carry the same General, FTA and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, split or renumbered.

changes.title: China Section 301 List 3 continues
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018 China Section 301 actions, so they stay in effect during the four-year review. For Chapter 55 this keeps +25% (9903.88.03) on every subheading except 5504.10.00 and 5513.21.00.

changes.title: Canadian import bans do not reach Chapter 55
changes.detail: Proclamations 11061–11063 banned some Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy-scope products and motorcycles over 800 cc from September 29, 2026. No Chapter 55 line is on their annexes, so Canadian retail yarn and dyed polyester fabric keep paying the 50% Section 338 duty.

changes.title: Section 338 list revised; 5511.10 and 5512.19 stay on it
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 added and deleted products on the 9903.03.14 list from September 15, 2026. Neither Chapter 55 subheading (5511.10.00, 5512.19.00) was removed, and none was added; Revision 21 still lists both in U.S. note 51(b)(3).

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty of 50% on retail yarn and dyed polyester fabric
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 put a 50% duty (9903.03.14) on Canadian goods in the provisions of U.S. note 51(b)(3), which include retail-packed yarn of 85% or more synthetic staple fiber (5511.10.00) and dyed, printed or yarn-dyed fabric of 85% or more polyester staple fiber (5512.19.00) — 13 statistical lines. It is charged even when USMCA is claimed and on top of the 10% Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods. Planned for August 19, it took effect August 22 after a 3-day suspension (Proclamation 11056).

changes.title: Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies reach every Chapter 55 line
changes.detail: 10% or 12.5% on all products of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84); no Chapter 55 subheading is on the general exemption list (note 52(b)). EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% in total and Japanese and Korean goods 12.5% in total where the base rate is lower. Jordan's exception list covers the chapter, Guatemala's and El Salvador's cover it with a CAFTA-DR claim, and CAFTA-DR textile goods entered duty-free are exempt (note 52(i)); USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94). Other FTA claims remove the base rate but not this duty.

changes.title: Section 122 import surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day surcharge (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on products of Brazil
changes.detail: 25% on all goods of Brazil (9903.05.01). No Chapter 55 subheading is on Brazil's exemption list (U.S. note 50(a)(ii), 9903.05.03). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 action (9903.05.27) is added on top.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: CBP forced-labor guidance for importers
changes.detail: CBP's operational guidance lists supply-chain tracing documents for the UFLPA high-priority sectors, including cotton and cotton products and apparel. Polyester-cotton yarn and fabric fall under the cotton tracing guidance, and the UFLPA presumption applies to goods of any kind made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by a listed entity.

changes.title: USITC starts mid-term review of the fine-denier PSF safeguard
changes.detail: The USITC instituted its monitoring investigation (TA-201-78) of the domestic fine denier polyester staple fiber industry; its report to the President and Congress is due by November 23, 2026, the mid-point of the safeguard. The safeguard can be reduced, modified or ended after that report.

changes.title: Low melt PSF from Korea: review rate set at 3.02%
changes.detail: Commerce's final results of the 2023–2024 antidumping review of low melt polyester staple fiber from Korea (5503.20.00.15) set a 3.02% margin for Toray Advanced Materials Korea. The order on Taiwan (49.93% at the order) also continues.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: 10% on products of all countries (9903.03.01) until July 23, 2026. No Chapter 55 subheading was on the product exemption list (9903.03.03). USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico were exempt (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08).

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24. The 9903.01.xx and 9903.02.xx headings are still printed in Revision 21 but are no longer in effect.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: Nicaragua Section 301 tariff phases in from 2027
changes.detail: USTR's action on Nicaragua adds a duty on all Nicaraguan goods that do not originate under CAFTA-DR (9903.89.01): 0% in 2026, 10% from January 1, 2027 and 15% from January 1, 2028. It reaches every Chapter 55 line; CAFTA-DR originating fabric and yarn are not affected.

changes.title: Fine-denier PSF safeguard: second-year quota opens
changes.detail: The quota on fine denier polyester staple fiber entered under a temporary importation bond (9903.55.01, U.S. note 32) rose from 0 kg to 453,592 kg for November 23, 2025 – November 22, 2026. It rises to 907,185 kg on November 23, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%. It applied to every Chapter 55 line on top of the Section 301 duties until it ended on February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) over India's purchases of Russian oil, on top of the 25% reciprocal rate in force since August 7, 2025 (EO 14326): 50% in all on Indian fiber, yarn and fabric. Ended February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 replaced the 10% baseline with country rates: India +25%, Taiwan and Vietnam +20%, Indonesia, Pakistan and Thailand +19%, South Korea and Türkiye +15%, and 15% in total for EU goods (Japan from September). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 (signed July 30, 2025) added 40% on goods of Brazil, on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada additional duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: Raised the IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods to +35% (9903.01.10). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Reciprocal tariff on products of all countries
changes.detail: 10% baseline (9903.01.25) and country rates (9903.02.xx); Canada and Mexico excluded. No Chapter 55 subheading was on the general exemption list. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China fentanyl duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.20, then 9903.01.24) went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the Section 301 duties.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.01); USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.04). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Additional duty on products of Canada
changes.detail: +25% on non-USMCA goods (9903.01.10), later raised to +35%; USMCA-qualifying goods exempt (9903.01.14). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 201 safeguard on fine denier polyester staple fiber
changes.detail: Proclamation 10857 (signed November 8, 2024) set a four-year quota on fine denier PSF (under 3.3 decitex) admitted free under a temporary importation bond (9813.00.05.20), starting at 0 kg. The USITC found increased imports a substantial cause of serious injury; the proclamation targets bonded entries, which it said undermined the existing antidumping and countervailing duty orders. Ordinary consumption entries are not limited. Korea is covered; Canada, Mexico, most FTA partners and developing countries are excluded.

changes.title: Fine denier PSF antidumping and countervailing orders continued
changes.detail: After the first five-year (sunset) reviews, Commerce continued the antidumping orders on fine denier polyester staple fiber from China, India, Korea and Taiwan and the countervailing duty orders on China and India (5503.20.00.25). Order rates: China-wide AD 103.06%, India 21.43%, Korea 45.23% (30.15% all-others), Taiwan 48.86% (24.43% all-others); CVD China 42.66% and India 24.80% all-others.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 55 goods were **$1.56B in 2025**, down 10% from $1.73B in 2024 and well below the 2022 peak of $2.14B. No supplier dominates: **South Korea $177.5M** (11%), **Türkiye $156.3M** (10%), **India $149.7M** (-27%), **Thailand $135.4M**, **Germany $110.3M** and **Vietnam $108.5M** (+31%, the only large supplier that grew). China fell 32% to $96.3M.

Fiber is the trade: staple fiber not yet spun (5503–5504) was 62% of the total. **Polyester staple fiber** (5503.20) was $491.6M (32%, down 15%) — Korea, Thailand and Vietnam were the largest suppliers of heading 5503 — and **viscose staple fiber** (5504.10) $213.1M; Germany, Indonesia and Austria shipped 63% of heading 5504. Retail-packed acrylic yarn (5511.10, $123.1M) came mainly from Türkiye; spun yarn (5509) was $120.1M and woven fabrics (5512–5516) $247.7M.

Through 2025 most suppliers paid the IEEPA tariffs — 50% on Indian goods from August 27 — on top of the base rate, Chinese goods the Section 301 duties as well, and polyester staple fiber from China, India, Korea and Taiwan its antidumping deposits. The IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026; since July 24, 2026 a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% applies instead. 2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data.

industryAreas.intro:
The total rate on Chapter 55 goods depends on **where they come from** as much as on what they are. Each cell below is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duty for that country, minus any preference — computed from the current tariff schedule with the same engine as the tariff calculator.

Since the IEEPA duties ended on February 24, 2026, the extra duty is mainly the **Section 301 tariff on 60 economies** (from July 24, 2026). **Japan pays 12.5% in total** and **the EU and Taiwan 10% in total** where the base rate is lower — so their fiber pays 10%–12.5% and most of their fabric just the base rate — **Korea 12.5%** on every line, while **Türkiye, Thailand and Vietnam pay 12.5%** and **India, Indonesia and Pakistan 10%** on top. **China and Brazil pay 37.5% more** on nearly every line, **Canada pays 50%** on retail yarn and dyed polyester fabric even with USMCA, and **Honduran and other CAFTA-DR textiles** entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR pay nothing extra. Antidumping and countervailing duties on polyester staple fiber come on top and are not in the grid.

tariffEngineering.h1: Importing Man-Made Staple Fibers, Yarn & Fabric (HTS Ch. 55): Origin Rules, AD/CVD, Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Polyester Staple Fiber, Spun Yarn & Fabric: Origin Rules, AD/CVD, Safeguard & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Chapter 55) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The CBP, Commerce and FTC rules for each HTS Chapter 55 line — textile country of origin (19 CFR 102.21), manufacturer ID, invoices and labeling, polyester staple fiber AD/CVD orders and the Section 201 TIB quota — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, CAFTA-DR, exception lists, the China viscose exclusion, TIB, samples and drawback.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Man-made fibers are textiles, so **CBP's textile rules decide where they come from**: tow and staple fiber are from where the polymer was extruded (cutting tow into staple does not change origin), yarn from where it was spun, and fabric from where it was woven — dyeing or printing alone does not move origin (19 CFR 102.21). Every entry names the manufacturer through a manufacturer identification code, and polyester staple fiber must be checked against **eleven antidumping and countervailing duty orders**.

The ways to pay less are in the schedule: claim **USMCA** or **CAFTA-DR** on regional fiber, yarn and fabric, source from **Jordan** (exception list) or a supplier outside the AD/CVD orders, claim China's **viscose-fiber exclusion**, enter goods for processing and re-export under a **temporary importation bond**, enter **samples** under Chapter 98, and claim **drawback** on re-exports. Each depends on a document, listed below with its regulation.

levers.title: Claim USMCA on fiber, yarn or fabric made in Mexico or Canada
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 25%) plus the 10% Section 301 duty for Mexico or Canada
levers.appliesTo: All 399 lines, for originating goods: staple fiber and yarn made from non-cotton, non-filament inputs in the region (fiber-forward), fabric woven from regional yarn (yarn-forward) — General Note 11, Chapter 55 rules
levers.document: A certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, in any format, with the SPI "S" on the entry line.
levers.caveat: For Canada, USMCA does not remove the 50% Section 338 duty on retail yarn (5511.10) and dyed polyester fabric (5512.19). The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

levers.title: Claim CAFTA-DR on yarn and fabric from Central America or the Dominican Republic
levers.saves: The base rate and the whole 10%–12.5% Section 301 duty
levers.appliesTo: All lines, for originating goods of Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua entered duty-free under CAFTA-DR (U.S. note 52(i), 9903.05.95; Guatemala and El Salvador also 52(j))
levers.document: A CAFTA-DR claim (SPI "P") supported by origin records; textile goods follow the yarn-forward rules of General Note 29.
levers.caveat: Non-originating goods pay the Section 301 duty, and so do lines already Free at the general rate (no CAFTA-DR rate to claim, e.g. fiber waste of 5505). From January 1, 2027 non-CAFTA Nicaraguan goods pay a further 10% (9903.89.01).

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(i), (j)

levers.title: Source from Jordan, whose exception list covers the chapter
levers.saves: The whole 10% Section 301 duty, and the base rate with a JO claim
levers.appliesTo: Every Chapter 55 subheading of Jordanian origin (U.S. note 52(j)(13), 9903.06.20)
levers.document: Proof of Jordanian origin (manufacturer ID, production records) and the exemption heading on the entry line; the U.S.–Jordan FTA (SPI "JO") for the Free base rate.
levers.caveat: Origin follows 19 CFR 102.21: fabric is from where it was woven and yarn from where it was spun, so finishing imported fabric in Jordan does not make it Jordanian.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(j)(13)

levers.title: Claim an FTA rate where the base rate is the cost
levers.saves: The base rate: up to 14.9% on most fabrics, 7%–13.2% on yarn, 4.3% on staple fiber
levers.appliesTo: All dutiable lines, for goods of Korea, Australia, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Panama, Israel, Morocco, Bahrain, Oman and Singapore
levers.document: Proof of origin under the agreement and the SPI on the entry line (KR, AU, CL, CO, PE, PA, IL, MA, BH, OM, SG).
levers.caveat: FTA claims do not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)); Korea pays 12.5% in total whatever the KORUS rate. GSP does not cover these textiles, and AGOA and Haiti HOPE/HELP benefits cover apparel, not staple fiber, yarn or fabric.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(a)

levers.title: Report the China List 4A exclusion on viscose staple fiber
levers.saves: The 7.5% List 4A duty (the 12.5% 2026 duty still applies)
levers.appliesTo: Chinese viscose rayon staple fiber, not carded or combed (5504.10.00.00), entered by November 9, 2026
levers.document: Heading 9903.88.69 reported with 5504.10.00.00 on the entry line.
levers.caveat: The exclusion ends after November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends it again; other cellulosic fiber (5504.90) pays List 3's 25%.

levers.title: Check the AD/CVD scope before buying polyester staple fiber
levers.saves: Antidumping and countervailing cash deposits — up to 103% AD and 42.66% CVD on Chinese fine denier PSF
levers.appliesTo: 5503.20 polyester staple fiber: fine denier under 3.3 decitex (China, India, Korea, Taiwan), 3.3 decitex or more (China, Korea, Taiwan) and low-melt bi-component fiber (Korea, Taiwan)
levers.document: Mill certificates showing denier, cut length and construction, and the producer and exporter names; a Commerce scope ruling (19 CFR 351.225) where coverage is unclear.
levers.caveat: Origin of staple fiber is where it was extruded, so fiber cut or baled elsewhere from Chinese tow is still Chinese. Excluded from the PSF orders: 10–18 denier fiber cut to 6–8 inches for carpet, and low-melt fiber (under its own order). Rates are company-specific and change after each review.

levers.title: Enter fiber, yarn or fabric for processing and re-export under a temporary importation bond
levers.saves: All duty, including the Section 301, China and Canada duties, on goods exported within the bond period
levers.appliesTo: Goods to be processed in the United States and then exported (9813.00.05)
levers.document: A TIB entry with a bond for twice the estimated duties; export within one year (extendable to three).
levers.caveat: Fine denier PSF (5503.20.00.25) entered under bond counts against the Section 201 quota (453,592 kg until November 22, 2026) unless it is from an excluded country. Goods not exported in time owe liquidated damages under the bond.

provisions.text: Articles to be repaired, altered or processed (including processes which result in articles manufactured or produced in the United States)

levers.title: Get a binding classification ruling where fiber content or weight decides the rate
levers.saves: Up to 25 points of base rate, and certainty on the China and Canada lists: staple vs. filament (chapter 55 vs. 54); polyester vs. cotton predominance (chapter 55 vs. 52); 85% thresholds (5512 vs. 5513–5515); 170 g/m² (5513 vs. 5514); wool content of 36% or more (25%)
levers.appliesTo: Any line where fiber content, weight, put-up or construction is in doubt — especially blends
levers.document: A ruling request to CBP describing fiber content by weight, weight per m², weave, yarn type and finish (19 CFR part 177); invoices must state the same details (19 CFR 141.89).
levers.caveat: Rulings apply to the transaction described; a different blend or construction may need its own.

levers.title: Enter swatches and fiber samples as samples
levers.saves: All duty — base rate and the Section 301, China and Canada duties
levers.appliesTo: Fabric swatches, yarn and fiber samples valued at $1 or less each, or marked, torn or perforated so they cannot be sold, used only to solicit orders
levers.document: Entry under 9811.00.60 with the samples marked or mutilated as the heading requires.
levers.caveat: Usable cuts or sample yardage for production do not qualify. U.S. notes 20, 51 and 52 exempt goods properly entered under Chapter 98 from those extra duties.

provisions.text: Samples valued not over $1 each, or marked, torn, perforated or otherwise treated so they are unsuitable for sale, used only for soliciting orders for products of foreign countries

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. notes 20(a), 51, 52(a)

levers.title: Claim drawback when the fiber, yarn or fabric is exported or used in exported goods
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid, including Section 301 duties
levers.appliesTo: All lines, when the imported goods or substitutes are exported or used in manufacturing exported goods
levers.document: A drawback claim filed in ACE within 5 years of import, with records linking the import to the export.
levers.caveat: Only duties actually paid are refunded; manufacturing drawback needs a ruling or a general manufacturing ruling.

rules.title: Textile country of origin: tow from where it was extruded; staple fiber (5503–5507) by a change from another chapter other than chapter 54, so where the polymer was extruded; waste from where it was garnetted; yarn and thread from where they were spun; fabric from where it was woven, or where greige fabric was dyed and printed with two finishing operations
Manufacturer identification code (MID) of the company that performed the origin-conferring operation on every entry — this replaced the textile declaration, eliminated in 2011
Entry is denied for textiles from a company named by CITA in the Federal Register for illegal transshipment or for being unable to verify production
Invoice details: fiber content by weight; for yarn, single or plied, retail put-up, sewing thread or not, and filament or spun; for fabric, weave, weight per m² and finish
Textile Fiber Products Identification Act: fibers, yarns and fabrics sold onward must show generic fiber names and percentages ("65% polyester, 35% cotton") and the country where processed or made

UFLPA: goods made wholly or in part in Xinjiang or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List are presumed made with forced labor and excluded unless the importer rebuts it; polyester-cotton yarn and fabric fall under the cotton tracing guidance

Antidumping and countervailing duty orders on polyester staple fiber (5503.20): fine denier PSF from China, India, Korea and Taiwan (AD) and China and India (CVD); certain PSF of 3.3 decitex or more from China, Korea and Taiwan (AD); low melt PSF from Korea and Taiwan (AD). CBP collects cash deposits at the rate in effect at entry

Section 201 safeguard: fine denier PSF admitted under a temporary importation bond (9813.00.05.20) is limited to the quota in U.S. note 32 (453,592 kg for November 23, 2025 – November 22, 2026) unless from an excluded country

rules.title: Country-of-origin marking on the article or, for bulk fiber, yarn and piece goods, on its container

groups.label: Synthetic filament tow (nylon, polyester, acrylic, polypropylene)
groups.note: Tow takes the origin of the country where the filaments were extruded. Tow over 2 m with the chapter note 1 specifications; shorter tow is staple fiber of 5503 or 5504.

groups.label: Artificial filament tow (viscose, acetate)
groups.note: Origin is where the cellulosic filaments were extruded. Acetate tow for cigarette filters is classified here.

groups.label: Synthetic staple fibers, not carded or combed (polyester, acrylic, aramid, polypropylene)
groups.note: Staple fiber keeps the origin of the extrusion country — cutting tow (5501) into staple is no change of chapter. Polyester staple fiber (5503.20) is under eleven AD/CVD orders and, for fine denier entered under bond, the safeguard quota.

groups.label: Artificial staple fibers, not carded or combed (viscose rayon, lyocell)
groups.note: Origin is where the viscose or lyocell fiber was extruded. Chinese viscose staple fiber (5504.10.00.00) can claim the List 4A exclusion through November 9, 2026.

groups.label: Waste of man-made fibers (noils, yarn waste, garnetted stock)
groups.note: Waste takes the origin of the garnetting country, or else the origin of the goods before they became waste.

groups.label: Synthetic staple fibers, carded or combed (tops)
groups.note: Carding or combing does not change origin (no change of chapter); the fiber keeps its extrusion origin.

groups.label: Artificial staple fibers, carded or combed
groups.note: Carding or combing does not change origin; the fiber keeps its extrusion origin.

groups.label: Sewing thread of man-made staple fibers
groups.note: Sewing thread takes the origin of the country where it was spun. Invoices must say it is sewing thread (19 CFR 141.89).

groups.label: Yarn of synthetic staple fibers, not for retail sale (spun polyester, acrylic yarn)
groups.note: Yarn takes the origin of the country where it was spun. Invoices give fiber content, ply and whether spun or filament.

groups.label: Yarn of artificial staple fibers, not for retail sale (spun rayon yarn)
groups.note: Yarn takes the origin of the country where it was spun; rates split by blend and ply.

groups.label: Yarn of man-made staple fibers put up for retail sale
groups.note: Retail put-ups (Section XI note 4). 5511.10 is on Canada's Section 338 list. Fiber-content labels apply to yarn sold to consumers.

groups.label: Woven fabrics of 85% or more synthetic staple fibers
groups.note: Fabric takes the origin of the country where it was woven; dyeing and printing alone do not change it. Dyed 5512.19 fabric is on Canada's Section 338 list.

groups.label: Woven fabrics of synthetic staple fibers under 85%, mixed with cotton, up to 170 g/m²
groups.note: Woven origin. Polyester must predominate by weight, else the fabric is cotton (chapter 52). 5513.21 is on no China Section 301 list.

groups.label: Woven fabrics of synthetic staple fibers under 85%, mixed with cotton, over 170 g/m²
groups.note: Woven origin; over 170 g/m². Poly-cotton blends fall under CBP's cotton supply-chain guidance for the UFLPA.

groups.label: Other woven fabrics of synthetic staple fibers (blends with rayon, filament, wool)
groups.note: Woven origin. Blends with 36% or more wool pay up to 25%; a ruling settles the fiber split.

groups.label: Woven fabrics of artificial staple fibers (spun rayon, viscose)
groups.note: Woven origin. Spun rayon and lyocell fabrics; filament rayon fabric is chapter 54 (5408).

seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about man-made staple fibers: the HS code for polyester and viscose staple fiber, spun polyester yarn, sewing thread, poly-cotton and rayon fabric, the antidumping duty on Chinese polyester staple fiber and the fine denier PSF safeguard.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most common questions about importing man-made staple fibers into the U.S. — HS codes, tariffs by country, antidumping orders and entry rules. Each answer links to the page with the full detail.
keyTakeaways: Chapter 55 base rates run from Free to 25% — 4.3% on staple fiber, 7%–13.2% on spun yarn, mostly 12%–14.9% on woven fabric — and are unchanged since January 2025.

Since July 24, 2026 most suppliers pay a 10% or 12.5% Section 301 tariff; EU and Taiwanese goods pay 10% and Japanese goods 12.5% in total, so their higher-rated yarn and fabric pay only the base rate; Korean goods (Free under KORUS) pay 12.5% on every line.
China and Brazil pay 37.5% extra on nearly every line (China 12.5% on viscose fiber and 5513.21 fabric); Canada pays 50% under Section 338 on retail yarn and dyed polyester fabric, even with USMCA.
Polyester staple fiber from China, India, Korea and Taiwan is under eleven AD/CVD orders, and fine denier PSF entered under bond is capped by a Section 201 quota through November 2028.
The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026 and the Section 122 surcharge expired July 23, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for polyester staple fiber?
searchedAs: virgin polyester staple fiber hs code
recycled polyester staple fiber hs code
faqs.answer: Polyester staple fiber not carded or combed is 5503.20.00 (4.3%), with statistical suffixes for low-melt bi-component fiber (.15), fiber under 3.3 decitex (.25), 3.3–13.2 decitex (.45) and 13.2 decitex or more (.65). Recycled and virgin fiber share the code. Carded or combed polyester fiber is 5506.20 (5.7%); filament tow is 5501.20.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for viscose or lyocell staple fiber?
faqs.answer: Viscose rayon staple fiber, not carded or combed, is 5504.10.00.00 (4.3%); other artificial (cellulosic) staple fiber such as lyocell is 5504.90.00.00. Carded or combed artificial fiber is 5507.00.00. Chinese viscose staple fiber pays 12.5% extra rather than 37.5% while its List 4A exclusion lasts (through November 9, 2026).

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for acrylic, polypropylene and aramid staple fiber?
faqs.answer: Synthetic staple fiber not carded is heading 5503: aramid 5503.11, other nylon 5503.19, polyester 5503.20, acrylic or modacrylic 5503.30, polypropylene 5503.40 and other 5503.90 — 4.3%, except Free for vinyon and nylon-12 blends. The same fibers as continuous tow are heading 5501 (7.5%).

faqs.question: What is the difference between staple fiber and filament for classification?
searchedAs: polyester staple fiber vs polyester filament yarn
man made staple fibres hs code
faqs.answer: Staple fibers are short cut lengths that are spun into yarn; filaments are continuous. Staple fiber, spun yarn and fabric woven from spun yarn are chapter 55; filament yarn and fabric woven from filament yarn are chapter 54. Tow — parallel filaments over 2 m — is in 5501–5502 (chapter note 1).

faqs.question: What is the HS code for spun polyester yarn and polyester sewing thread?
searchedAs: spun polyester sewing thread hs code
faqs.answer: Spun yarn of 85% or more polyester staple fiber is 5509.21 (single, 9.7%) or 5509.22 (multiple, 10.6%); polyester mixed mainly with cotton is 5509.53 (13.2%). Sewing thread of man-made staple fiber is 5508.10 (11.4%). Yarn put up for retail sale is 5511 (7.5%). Filament polyester yarn and thread are chapter 54.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for polyester-cotton fabric?
searchedAs: cotton polyester blend fabric hs code
faqs.answer: The predominant fiber by weight decides (Section XI note 2). A woven fabric with more polyester staple than cotton, but under 85% polyester, is 5513 (170 g/m² or less) or 5514 (over 170 g/m²) — mostly 14.9%. A 65/35 polyester-cotton shirting is 5513. If cotton predominates, the fabric is chapter 52; 85% or more polyester is 5512.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for viscose or rayon fabric?
faqs.answer: Woven fabric of spun viscose or lyocell is heading 5516 — 14.9% for most unbleached or dyed 85%+ rayon fabric. Polyester-viscose blends where polyester predominates are 5515.11 (14.9%). Fabric woven from filament rayon is 5408 (chapter 54), and knitted fabric chapter 60.

faqs.question: What do HS codes 5512 and 5515 cover?
faqs.answer: 5512 is woven fabric of 85% or more synthetic staple fiber — 5512.11/.19 polyester (12% unbleached, 13.6% dyed or printed), 5512.21/.29 acrylic, 5512.91/.99 other. 5515 is other synthetic staple-fiber fabric: blends with rayon (5515.11), filament (5515.12) or wool (5515.13, up to 25%). Canadian 5512.19 fabric pays the 50% Section 338 duty.

faqs.question: What is the tariff and antidumping duty on polyester staple fiber from China?
searchedAs: anti dumping duty on polyester staple fiber from china
faqs.answer: Chinese polyester staple fiber pays 4.3% plus 25% (List 3) and 12.5% (2026 action): 41.8%. Fine denier fiber also owes an antidumping deposit (103.00% China-wide at the order) and a countervailing deposit (42.66% all-others); fiber of 3.3 decitex or more owes the 2007 order's deposit (44.30% PRC-wide). Company rates vary by review.

faqs.question: Which countries have antidumping duties on polyester staple fiber?
searchedAs: polyester staple fiber anti dumping duty
faqs.answer: Fine denier PSF (under 3.3 decitex): AD on China, India, Korea and Taiwan, CVD on China and India (2018, continued 2024). PSF of 3.3 decitex or more: AD on Korea and Taiwan (2000) and China (2007). Low melt PSF: AD on Korea and Taiwan (2018); Toray Advanced Materials Korea's 2023–2024 review rate is 3.02%. Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia are not covered.

faqs.question: What is the fine denier polyester staple fiber safeguard?
searchedAs: fine denier polyester staple fiber safeguard
faqs.answer: A Section 201 quota (Proclamation 10857) on fine denier PSF entered duty-free under a temporary importation bond: 0 kg in the year from November 23, 2024, 453,592 kg to November 22, 2026, then 907,185 kg and 1,360,777 kg through November 22, 2028. Ordinary entries are not limited. Korea is covered; Canada, Mexico and most FTA partners are not.

faqs.question: What tariffs apply to HTS Chapter 55 imports in 2026?
faqs.answer: The base rate plus, for most suppliers, a 10% or 12.5% Section 301 tariff since July 24, 2026 (EU and Taiwan 10%, Korea and Japan 12.5% in total). China and Brazil pay 37.5% extra, Canada 50% on 5511.10 and 5512.19, and USMCA, CAFTA-DR and Jordanian goods are exempt from Section 301. The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24 and the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import man-made staple fiber from?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the U.S. imported $1.56B of Chapter 55 goods: South Korea $177.5M, Türkiye $156.3M, India $149.7M, Thailand $135.4M, Germany $110.3M and Vietnam $108.5M, then China $96.3M. Korea, Thailand and Vietnam ship mostly polyester staple fiber; Germany and Austria viscose fiber; Türkiye acrylic retail yarn.

faqs.question: How is the country of origin of man-made fiber, yarn and fabric determined?
searchedAs: man made fiber country of origin
faqs.answer: By CBP's textile rules (19 CFR 102.21): staple fiber is from where the polymer was extruded, yarn from where it was spun and fabric from where it was woven — dyeing and printing alone do not change it unless greige fabric is both dyed and printed with two further finishing steps. Origin decides the Section 301 rate and AD/CVD coverage.

faqs.question: Do USMCA and CAFTA-DR fabrics and yarns pay the 2026 Section 301 tariff?
faqs.answer: No, if they qualify: USMCA goods are exempt (9903.05.93, 9903.05.94) and CAFTA-DR textile goods entered duty-free are exempt (note 52(i)). Qualifying yarn must be spun from regional fiber and fabric woven from regional yarn. Canadian retail yarn (5511.10) and dyed polyester fabric (5512.19) still pay 50% under Section 338.
